title: Nursing Note - Admission to Step-Down
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: 82 y/o F POD 0 right hip ORIF arrived from PACU on 2 L NC with post-op anemia (Hgb 7.9); PRBC to start 1930.
body:
**Situation**
Doris Kowalczyk, 82 y/o F, arrived to SD-12 at 1820 from PACU after right intertrochanteric femur ORIF with cephalomedullary nail (Dr. Reyes, spinal anesthesia, EBL 350 mL). Full Code. Allergy: sulfa (rash). Weight 61 kg.

**Background / Report from PACU RN**
Post-op hypotension (BP 86/48, HR 112) treated with LR 500 mL bolus; Hgb 7.9 at 1630. History HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis. Cefazolin 2 g IV given 1400; next dose 2200.

**Assessment**
- Vitals 1830: T 97.8 F, HR 102, BP 100/58, RR 20, SpO2 93% on 2 L NC, pain 5/10.
- Neuro: drowsy but easily arousable, oriented x4, follows commands. Glasses and left hearing aid on.
- CV: sinus tachycardia on telemetry, no ectopy. Cap refill brisk.
- Resp: lungs clear, unlabored. Oxygen 2 L/min NC started 1830, titrate to SpO2 92% or higher. Incentive spirometer taught.
- Right leg neurovascular: foot warm, DP/PT pulses palpable, cap refill under 3 sec, sensation and toe movement intact.
- Incision right lateral thigh: Aquacel dressing dry and intact, no drainage; no thigh swelling.
- GU: Foley 16 Fr (placed Saturday 2330, catheter day 2) draining clear yellow urine, bag below bladder, secured to thigh.
- PIV 20 g left forearm patent, no LR running at present.
- Pain: right hip 5/10, aching; oxycodone PRN available, repositioned with pillow between legs.
- Safety: fall precautions, bed alarm on, call light in reach, non-skid socks. SCD to left leg only.

**Plan**
- PRBC 1 unit to start 1930 (consent verified, 2-RN check, baseline vitals before start).
- Hgb recheck after transfusion; neurovascular checks q4h; strict I&O; vitals per order.
- Cefazolin 2200. Updated patient on plan; daughter Karen Mills called with update.

title: Nursing Note - Transfusion Completed
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: 1 unit PRBC completed 2300 without reaction; Hgb recheck due 2330.
body:
**Transfusion**
1 unit PRBC started 1930 (pre-transfusion vitals 1930: T 97.9 F, HR 100, BP 102/60, RR 20, SpO2 94% on 2 L). Rate titrated to complete over 3.5 hours. Completed 2300. Line flushed with normal saline.

**Vitals during and after**
- 1945 (15 min): T 98.0 F, HR 99, BP 104/60, RR 20, SpO2 94%.
- 2100: T 98.2 F, HR 96, BP 108/62, RR 19, SpO2 94%.
- 2300: T 98.4 F, HR 92, BP 112/64, RR 18, SpO2 94% on 2 L NC, pain 4/10.

No chills, rigors, hives, back or flank pain, dyspnea or fever. Lungs clear, no new edema. HR trending down and BP trending up after transfusion.

**Other**
- Cefazolin 2 g IV given at 2200 as scheduled.
- Right foot warm, pulses present, sensation and toe movement intact. Dressing dry and intact.
- Foley draining clear yellow urine; output being tracked hourly.
- Pain 4/10; resting comfortably, oriented x4.

**Plan**
- Post-transfusion Hgb recheck at 2330.
- Continue vitals per order, neurovascular checks q4h, bed alarm, telemetry, oxygen 2 L.
- Report to provider if Hgb remains low or any delayed reaction signs.

title: Nursing Note - Day Shift Assessment
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: POD 1 day shift assessment: hemodynamically recovered, on 2 L NC, Foley in for strict I&O.
body:
**Report**
Received report from P. Dalton, RN at 0700. Quiet night, Hgb 9.2 this AM after transfusion.

**Vitals 0700**
T 98.4 F, HR 88, BP 116/66, RR 18, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC, pain 4/10.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: alert, oriented x4, calm. Glasses and left hearing aid on.
- CV: regular rhythm on telemetry, HR 80s. BP recovered from yesterday's hypotension. Lisinopril held per orders.
- Resp: lungs clear bilaterally, 2 L NC; incentive spirometry coached.
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation and toe movement intact. Aquacel dressing dry and intact, no drainage.
- GI: abdomen soft, tolerating diet, no BM yet.
- GU: Foley (catheter day 3) draining clear yellow urine; 0300-0700 in 520 mL, out 320 mL (80 mL/h, 1.3 mL/kg/h). Foley being kept for strict I&O.
- IV: LR 75 mL/h running via L forearm PIV.
- Labs 0530: WBC 10.2, Hgb 9.2, creatinine 1.3. Glucose 156 at 0730.
- Skin intact; heels floated. SCD left leg in bed.

**Plan**
- Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ due 0900. PT to evaluate for first stand and bed-to-chair.
- Room air trial as tolerated; continue fall precautions with bed alarm; strict I&O.

title: Nursing Note - PT First Stand and Bed-to-Chair
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: First stand with PT and bed-to-chair transfer tolerated; room air trial failed earlier.
body:
**Mobility**
With S. Kim, PT, patient sat at the edge of the bed, then stood with a walker and 1 assist, weight-bearing as tolerated on the right leg. Pivoted to a chair, sat about 45 minutes. Pain 5/10 with standing, 4/10 once seated. No dizziness; BP stable.

**Vitals 1100**
T 98.6 F, HR 90, BP 118/68, RR 18, SpO2 94% on 2 L NC, pain 5/10.

**Respiratory**
Brief room air trial this morning: SpO2 fell below the 92% goal within a few minutes, so 2 L NC was resumed with recovery. Will retry later. Incentive spirometry encouraged.

**Other**
- Right foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact; dressing dry and intact (first dressing check done, no drainage, no swelling).
- Foley (catheter day 3) draining clear yellow urine. 0700-1100 in 580 mL, out 300 mL (75 mL/h, 1.2 mL/kg/h).
- Glucose 172 at 1130. Diet advanced; ate about 60% of lunch tray in chair.
- Lisinopril still held.

**Plan**
- Chair for meals; return to bed with 1 assist and bed alarm.
- Scheduled acetaminophen 1400; continue fall precautions.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Assessment
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: POD 1 evening assessment: stable vitals, on 2 L NC, Foley draining clear yellow.
body:
**Report**
Report received from L. Okoye, RN at 1900. Day shift: first stand and chair with PT, BP recovered, room air trial failed.

**Vitals 1900**
T 98.6 F, HR 86, BP 122/68, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC, pain 4/10.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: alert, oriented x4, appropriate, good cooperation with care.
- CV: regular rhythm on telemetry, no ectopy. Lisinopril held.
- Resp: lungs clear, 2 L NC, IS used with 1,000 mL.
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation and toe movement intact; Aquacel dry and intact.
- GI: eating well, BM this afternoon; senna-docusate and Miralax scheduled.
- GU: Foley (catheter day 3) draining clear yellow urine. 1500-1900 in 600 mL, out 280 mL (70 mL/h, 1.15 mL/kg/h). Glucose 148 at 1630.
- IV: LR 75 mL/h, L forearm PIV site clean, no redness.
- Skin: intact, repositioned.

**Safety**
Bed alarm on, call light in reach, non-skid socks, glasses and hearing aid within reach.

**Plan**
- Vitals q4h, neurovascular checks q4h, strict I&O, glucose at HS.
- Acetaminophen 2200; PRN oxycodone as needed; atorvastatin HS.
- Reassess need for Foley with provider in AM.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Summary
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: Quiet night, pain 4/10, Foley output about 57 mL/h, glucose 176 at 2100.
body:
**Overnight summary**
Quiet night. Slept in 2 to 3 hour blocks, easily woken for care and repositioned q2h.

**Vitals 0300**
T 98.4 F, HR 86, BP 118/66, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC, pain 4/10.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: oriented x4, no confusion, calm.
- Resp: lungs clear, 2 L NC, SpO2 stayed 94 to 95%.
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation and toe movement intact at all q4h checks. Dressing dry and intact.
- Pain: 4/10 hip ache; scheduled acetaminophen 1,000 mg given 2200; no PRN opioid needed overnight.
- GU: Foley (catheter day 4) draining clear yellow urine. 1900-2300 in 500 mL, out 240 mL (60 mL/h, 0.98 mL/kg/h); 2300-0300 in 380 mL, out 230 mL (57 mL/h, 0.94 mL/kg/h).
- Glucose 176 at 2100 (bedtime), within range for patient.
- LR 75 mL/h infusing, PIV site clean.

**Plan**
- Labs (CBC, BMP) at 0500; levothyroxine and acetaminophen at 0600.
- Continue bed alarm, q4h vitals and neurovascular checks, telemetry.
- Report to day RN at 0700.

title: Nursing Note - Day Shift Assessment
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: POD 2 assessment, all systems stable; Foley is catheter day 4 and provider review of need is due.
body:
**Report**
Received from P. Dalton, RN at 0700: quiet night, no PRN opioids, no concerns.

**Vitals 0700**
T 98.6 F, HR 88, BP 118/66, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC, pain 4/10. Glucose 142 at 0730.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: alert, oriented x4, pleasant.
- CV: regular rhythm on telemetry, HR 80s. Lisinopril held; plan to resume after Wednesday creatinine.
- Resp: lungs clear; SpO2 95% on 2 L; IS 1,000 mL.
- GI: abdomen soft, eating; last BM Monday.
- GU: Foley 16 Fr draining clear yellow urine. 0300-0700 in 380 mL, out 260 mL (65 mL/h, 1.07 mL/kg/h).
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact, toe movement intact. Incision right lateral thigh, Aquacel dry and intact, no drainage.
- Skin intact. SCD left leg in bed.
- Labs 0500: WBC 11.2, Hgb 9.0, creatinine 1.3, K 4.1, glucose 154.
- IV: LR 75 mL/h via L forearm PIV; stops at 0900.

**Foley**
Today is catheter day 4 (placed Saturday 2330). Provider order review for continued need is due; will ask Dr. Patel at rounds whether strict output still requires the catheter.

**Plan**
- Enoxaparin 0900. PT/OT at 0900 with oxycodone premedication at 0830. Fall precautions with bed alarm.

title: Nursing Note - PT/OT Mobility
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: Stood and walked 10 ft with walker and 1 assist; pain 6/10 with activity.
body:
**Mobility**
Oxycodone 5 mg PO given 0830 for pain 6/10 before therapy. With PT and OT, patient sat at the edge of bed, then stood with walker and 1 assist and walked 10 ft, weight-bearing as tolerated on right leg. Fatigued after the walk, rested in chair.

**Vitals 0900**
T 98.6 F, HR 86, BP 120/68, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC, pain 6/10 with activity (4/10 at rest afterward).

**Other**
- LR 75 mL/h stopped at 0900, drinking well; PIV locked and flushed.
- Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ given at 0900. Lisinopril held per plan.
- Incentive spirometry 1,000 mL at 1000.
- Dietitian saw patient: protein supplement BID added. Case management reviewing SNF referral; Maple Grove expected to respond at 1400.
- Right foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact. Dressing dry and intact.
- Foley draining clear yellow urine.
- Daughter Karen Mills arrived and sat with patient.

**Plan**
- Chair for lunch, up with 1 assist and walker.
- Wean oxygen as tolerated, goal trial later today; fall precautions.

title: Nursing Note - Midday
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: Midday status: stable vitals, oxycodone 1300 for pain, glucose 138, daughter visiting.
body:
**Vitals 1300**
T 98.8 F, HR 84, BP 122/70, RR 17, SpO2 95% on 2 L NC, pain 4/10 (5/10 before 1300 dose).

**Assessment**
- Neuro: alert, oriented x4, conversing with daughter Karen Mills, who is at bedside.
- Resp: lungs clear, SpO2 steady on 2 L. Plan a room air trial at 1400.
- Nutrition: ate about 70% of lunch in chair plus protein supplement. Drinking water and juice. 0700-1100 in 640 mL, out 250 mL (62 mL/h, 1.02 mL/kg/h).
- Glucose 138 at 1130, no correction required.
- GU: Foley draining clear yellow urine.
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact. Dressing dry and intact.
- Pain: oxycodone 2.5 mg PO given at 1300 for pain 5/10 (right hip).

**Plan**
- Acetaminophen 1,000 mg due 1400.
- Room air trial at 1400 with SpO2 check; if above 92%, discontinue oxygen.
- Back to bed with bed alarm for rest; incentive spirometry hourly.
- Continue fall precautions.

title: Nursing Note - Afternoon
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: Room air since 1400, SpO2 94%; cloudy, stronger-smelling urine at catheter care and slightly more tired.
body:
**Respiratory**
Oxygen discontinued at 1400. Room air since 1400, SpO2 94% (T 98.9 F, HR 86, BP 124/68, RR 17 at 1400). Lungs clear, no dyspnea.

**Vitals 1500**
T 99.3 F, HR 88, BP 122/68, RR 18, SpO2 94% RA, pain 4/10.

**Catheter care at 1500**
Perineal and catheter care done. Urine in tubing and bag is slightly cloudy with a stronger odor than this morning (was clear yellow earlier). Catheter secure, no kinking, no leaking or meatal redness. Output 1100-1500: in 560 mL, out 240 mL (60 mL/h, 0.98 mL/kg/h). She seems a little more tired than earlier, but oriented and conversing with Karen. Encouraged oral fluids; water at bedside.

**Other**
- Acetaminophen 1,000 mg given at 1400.
- Maple Grove accepted the SNF referral at 1400 per case management.
- Right foot warm, pulses present; dressing dry and intact.

**Plan**
- Recheck temperature at 1700 and keep monitoring urine appearance, mental status and intake.
- Tell the night nurse at handoff about the urine and the temperature trend.

title: Nursing Note - End of Shift Handoff
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: End of day shift SBAR: low-grade temperature trend, brief confusion at dinner; Foley still in.
body:
**Situation**
Doris Kowalczyk, POD 2, Full Code, sulfa allergy. Stable overall but temperature is creeping up and she had brief confusion at dinner.

**Background**
Right hip ORIF Sunday. Room air since 1400. Foley in since Saturday 2330 (day 4). Urine slightly cloudy and stronger-smelling at 1500 care.

**Assessment**
- Temp: 99.4 F at 1700, 99.6 F at 1800 (was 98.6 F this morning). 1800 HR 92, BP 118/66, RR 18, SpO2 94% RA, pain 4/10.
- Neuro: at dinner at 1800 she asked where her husband was (widow). Reoriented gently to place and situation; again oriented x4 within minutes. Glasses and hearing aid on.
- I&O block 1500-1900 (totaled at end of shift): intake 480 mL; output 220 mL (55 mL/h, 0.90 mL/kg/h).
- Glucose 154 at 1630, lispro 2 units given. Oxycodone 2.5 mg at 1700.
- Right foot warm, pulses present; dressing dry and intact. Lungs clear.
- Daughter Karen Mills left; aware of the changes.

**Recommendation / SBAR to night RN P. Dalton**
- Watch temperature and mental status closely; repeat vitals early in the shift.
- Foley still in; watch urine appearance and push fluids.
- Bed alarm, toileting, reorient as needed; escalate if temperature rises or confusion returns.

title: Nursing Note - Night Shift Assessment
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: Evening assessment: T 100.1 F at 2000, HR 94, restless and picking at the Foley.
body:
**Report**
Received report from L. Okoye, RN at 1900: temperature trending up, brief confusion at dinner, Foley still in.

**Vitals**
1900: T 99.8 F, HR 92, BP 118/66, RR 18, SpO2 94% RA.
2000: T 100.1 F, HR 94, BP 116/64, RR 19, SpO2 94% RA, pain 5/10.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: awake, restless, repeatedly pulling at the bedding and picking at the Foley tubing. States "I need to go." Oriented to person but needed reminders about place. Glasses and left hearing aid on.
- GU: Foley in place, secure, no kinks, bag below bladder. Urine cloudy, dark yellow in tubing.
- Resp: lungs clear, no cough, unlabored on room air.
- CV: HR 94 regular on telemetry.
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact. Dressing dry and intact.
- Pain 5/10 hip; repositioned.

**Safety**
Fall precautions: bed alarm on, call light in reach, low bed, non-skid socks, frequent rounding. Assured her the catheter is in place and the bladder is being drained.

**Plan**
- Recheck vitals and glucose at 2100, full reassessment including mental status.
- Offer oral fluids; scheduled acetaminophen due 2200.
- Notify provider if temperature or confusion worsens.

title: Nursing Note - Change in Condition SBAR
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: New fever, tachycardia and confusion; Dr. Ahmed notified at 2115 with orders for UA, cultures, labs and Foley removal.
body:
**Situation**
At 2100, T 100.8 F, HR 102, new confusion (CAM positive).

**Background**
82 y/o F POD 2 right hip ORIF, Foley catheter day 4 (placed Saturday 2330). Temperature trended 99.3 F (1500), 99.6 F (1800), 100.1 F (2000). Urine cloudy, stronger odor. Sulfa allergy.

**Assessment 2100**
- Vitals: T 100.8 F, HR 102, BP 112/62, RR 20, SpO2 93% RA, pain 5/10.
- CAM positive: acute change, inattention, disorganized thinking, fluctuating alertness.
- Mild suprapubic discomfort to palpation; no flank pain, no cough, lungs clear. Incision clean, dressing dry and intact. Right foot neurovascularly intact.
- Glucose 188 at 2100; lispro 2 units given. Atorvastatin and senna-docusate given at 2100.

**Notification**
Dr. N. Ahmed called at 2115 with SBAR; verbalized understanding and gave orders.

**Orders received**
- UA with culture from the catheter sampling port
- Blood cultures x2, CBC, BMP, lactate
- Push oral fluids; strict I&O
- Remove Foley after the specimen is collected; bladder scan after removal
- Scheduled 2200 acetaminophen is due

**Plan**
Collect specimens before any antibiotics. Vitals q2h, reorient, bed alarm, quiet room. Update daughter Karen Mills in the morning unless condition changes.

title: Nursing Note - Specimen Collection and Foley Removal
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: Cultures collected, T 100.9 F, acetaminophen given at 2200, Foley removed at 2200.
body:
**Specimens**
- 2145: Urine for UA and culture collected aseptically from the catheter sampling port after cleaning with an alcohol pad (not from the bag). CBC, BMP and lactate drawn with it.
- 2150: Blood cultures x2, two separate peripheral sites, before any antibiotic.
All labeled at bedside and sent.

**Vitals**
2130: T 100.9 F, HR 104, BP 112/60, RR 20, SpO2 93% RA. 2200: T 100.9 F, HR 106, BP 110/60, RR 21, SpO2 93% RA. Temperature documented before the dose below. Note that acetaminophen can mask fever, so the trend must be read with the dose time in mind.

**Medication**
Scheduled acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO given at 2200 after the 2200 temperature recorded. PRN 650 mg order left unused.

**Foley removal**
Foley 16 Fr (catheter day 5) removed at 2200 per Dr. Ahmed, no further indication. Balloon deflated, catheter removed intact with tip intact, no resistance, no bleeding, patient tolerated well. Bag emptied and measured for I&O. Perineal care done.

**Fluids**
Oral fluids encouraged since 1900; water and juice offered each visit. Intake and output will be totaled for the 1900-2300 block.

**Plan**
- Bladder scan after removal and if no void; call provider for residual over 300 mL or no void within 6 hours.
- Toileting every 2 hours, bed alarm, reorient, monitor CAM and vitals q2h.

title: Nursing Note - Antibiotic Administration
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: UA positive, WBC 14.6; ceftriaxone 1 g IV given 2330 after cultures with no reaction.
body:
**Results**
- UA (2230): cloudy, dark yellow, leukocyte esterase large, nitrite positive, WBC more than 50/hpf, bacteria many.
- CBC: WBC 14.6, Hgb 9.0. BMP: creatinine 1.3, K 4.0, glucose 188. Lactate 1.5.
- Urine and blood cultures pending. Dr. Ahmed informed of results and ordered an antibiotic.

**Antibiotic**
Sulfa allergy (rash) verified on the armband and in the chart; no TMP-SMX. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV started at 2330, infusing over 30 minutes through the left forearm PIV, after cultures were collected. No rash, itching, flushing or shortness of breath so far. Site clean.

**Assessment**
- 2300: T 100.4 F, HR 100, BP 114/62, RR 20, SpO2 94% RA, pain 4/10.
- Glucose 188 at 2100, lispro 2 units given.
- CAM still positive: intermittently confused, redirectable. Not yet voided since catheter removal at 2200; bladder scan to follow.
- Mild suprapubic discomfort unchanged.

**Safety / Comfort**
Bed alarm on, toileting every 2 hours, quiet room with lights low, glasses and hearing aid within reach, no new sedatives. Oral fluids encouraged.

**Plan**
Vitals q2h; bladder scan, CAM recheck, strict I&O; next ceftriaxone dose due 2330 Wednesday.

title: Nursing Note - Overnight
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: T 99.6 F at 0200, first void 220 mL at 0215, post-void scan 80 mL, confusion improving.
body:
**Vitals**
0000: T 100.2 F, HR 98, BP 116/64. 0100: T 99.9 F, HR 94. 0200: T 99.6 F, HR 92, BP 120/66, RR 18, SpO2 95% RA, pain 3/10.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: confusion improving, now calmer, oriented to person and place, redirectable; CAM improving. Asleep now, easily arousable.
- GU: first void after catheter removal at 0215, 220 mL, clear to pale yellow, no burning reported. Bladder scan afterward: 80 mL residual. Voided spontaneously to bedside commode with 1 assist.
- Resp: lungs clear, no cough.
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact. Dressing dry and intact.
- Intake 2300-0200 on target; oral fluids encouraged.
- Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given at 2330, no adverse reaction.

**Safety**
Bed alarm on, call light in reach, toileting every 2 hours, quiet room, lights low.

**Plan**
- Vitals q2h until afebrile; 0500 labs; continue monitoring mental status and void pattern.
- Acetaminophen scheduled 0600.

title: Nursing Note - Early Morning
author: P. Dalton, RN
summary: Afebrile 98.9 F, confusion cleared (CAM negative), voiding, labs improving; handoff.
body:
**Vitals 0600**
T 98.9 F, HR 82, BP 128/70, RR 17, SpO2 96% RA, pain 3/10. Temperature trend overnight: 100.2 F (0000), 99.6 F (0200), 99.4 F (0300), 99.1 F (0500), 98.9 F (0600).

**Neuro**
CAM negative at 0600. Awake, oriented x4, conversant, appropriate. Slept 4 hours.

**Labs 0500**
WBC 12.1 (was 14.6), Hgb 9.3, creatinine 1.2, K 4.1, glucose 163.

**GU / I&O**
Voiding spontaneously after catheter removal; second void about 260 mL at 0445. 1900-2300 in 520 mL, out 200 mL; 2300-0300 in 450 mL, out 220 mL; 0300-0700 block still in progress. Output adequate with no retention. No dysuria reported.

**Other**
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact. Dressing dry and intact. Lungs clear.
- Scheduled acetaminophen 1,000 mg and levothyroxine 75 mcg given at 0600.
- Blood and urine cultures pending. Ceftriaxone next due 2330.
- Bed alarm on, toileting q2h continues.

**Handoff**
To day RN L. Okoye at 0700: telemetry to be discontinued per order after provider rounds, lisinopril to resume after creatinine review, glucose due 0730.

title: Nursing Note - Day Shift Assessment
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: Afebrile, oriented x4, voiding; telemetry off, enoxaparin due 0900, lisinopril to resume.
body:
**Report**
Received from P. Dalton, RN at 0700: febrile episode overnight resolved, confusion cleared, voiding.

**Vitals 0700**
T 98.8 F, HR 82, BP 128/70, RR 17, SpO2 96% on room air, pain 3/10. Glucose 168 at 0730; lispro 2 units given.

**Assessment**
- Neuro: alert, oriented x4, CAM negative, bright and conversant.
- CV: regular rhythm; telemetry discontinued per order with no arrhythmia during stay.
- Resp: lungs clear on room air.
- GU: voiding spontaneously, urine clear yellow. 0300-0700 in 380 mL, out 260 mL.
- Right leg: foot warm, pulses present, sensation and toe movement intact. Aquacel dressing dry and intact, no drainage.
- GI: abdomen soft; tolerating diet.
- Skin intact. IV: L forearm PIV locked, site clean.
- Labs 0500: WBC 12.1, Hgb 9.3, creatinine 1.2.

**Plan**
- Enoxaparin 40 mg due 0900; lisinopril 10 mg to resume (creatinine 1.2), hold if SBP under 110.
- PT/OT at 0900 with oxycodone premedication at 0830; monitor temperature, mental status and urination.
- Cultures pending; SNF transfer planned today.

title: Nursing Note - PT/OT Mobility
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: Walked 40 ft with walker and stand-by assist; toilet transfer with raised seat.
body:
**Mobility**
Oxycodone 2.5 mg PO given at 0830 for pain 5/10 before therapy. With PT and OT, walked 40 ft with a walker and stand-by assist, weight-bearing as tolerated on right leg, steady gait. OT worked on toilet transfer using a raised toilet seat; completed with stand-by assist and good safety awareness.

**Vitals 0900**
T 98.7 F, HR 80, BP 134/74, RR 17, SpO2 96% RA, pain 4/10 with activity, 3/10 at rest afterward.

**Other**
- Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ given 0900; calcium/vitamin D, senna-docusate and Miralax given at 0900. Lisinopril 10 mg given at 0930 with BP 134/74.
- Voiding spontaneously with each toileting trip, urine clear yellow.
- Right foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact. Dressing dry and intact.
- Oriented x4, no confusion, appropriate, motivated.

**Plan**
- Chair for rest and meals; up with walker and 1 assist.
- Continue hourly incentive spirometry and fall precautions.

title: Nursing Note - Results and Teaching
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: Cultures update, post-void scan 60 mL, teaching on catheter-associated UTI to patient and daughter.
body:
**Results**
- Blood cultures x2: no growth to date (0800, about 10 hours).
- Urine culture preliminary (0930): Gram-negative rods, more than 100,000 CFU/mL; identification and susceptibilities to follow after transfer.
- Glucose 152 at 1130; lispro 2 units given.

**Vitals 1100**
T 98.6 F, HR 78, BP 132/72, RR 16, SpO2 96% RA, pain 3/10.

**Assessment**
- Voided at 1100; bladder scan afterward 60 mL. Voiding about every 3 to 4 hours. 0700-1100 in 520 mL, out 300 mL.
- Ate 75% of breakfast. Oriented x4, calm, no burning or urgency.

**Teaching (patient and daughter Karen Mills)**
- Her urinary infection is likely related to the catheter. Preventing recurrence: wipe front to back, drink fluids through the day, hand hygiene.
- Report burning, urgency, new confusion or fever right away to nursing or SNF staff.
- Ceftriaxone will continue as IM injection once daily at the skilled nursing facility, next dose due tonight at 2330; the agent and total duration will be set from the final culture.
Both verbalized understanding and repeated back the warning signs.

**Plan**
Nurse-to-nurse report to Maple Grove at 1330; PIV to be removed before leaving.

title: Nursing Note - Transfer Preparation
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: Report given to C. Pruitt RN at Maple Grove at 1330; belongings and pending results reviewed.
body:
**Report**
Nurse-to-nurse report given by phone at 1330 to C. Pruitt, RN at Maple Grove Skilled Nursing and Rehabilitation using SBAR.

**Situation / Background**
82 y/o F, POD 3 right hip ORIF with cephalomedullary nail (WBAT right leg). Catheter-associated UTI recognized Tuesday night; Foley removed Tuesday 2200. Sulfa allergy. Full Code.

**Assessment (1300)**
T 98.6 F, HR 78, BP 130/72, RR 16, SpO2 96% RA, pain 3/10. Oriented x4. Voiding, bladder scan 60 mL at 1100. Dressing dry and intact, staples 3.

**Recommendations / handoff points**
- Ceftriaxone 1 g IM daily, next dose due tonight 2330 at SNF; first 3 days (Tue, Wed, Thu 2330), then agent and total duration per the final culture.
- Enoxaparin 40 mg SQ daily (last given 0900) to complete 35 days; metformin resumes; restart alendronate when upright 30 minutes.
- Labs Friday (BMP, CBC). PT/OT daily. Follow up with Dr. Reyes in 2 weeks, staples out.
- Pending: final urine culture identification and susceptibilities (Thursday); blood cultures final.
- Watch for fever, new confusion, burning or urgency.

**Belongings**
Glasses, left hearing aid and cane to go with her.

**Plan**
- PIV removal at 1415; scheduled acetaminophen at 1400.
- Daughter Karen Mills present; transport planned at 1430.

title: Nursing Note - Transfer to Skilled Nursing Facility
author: L. Okoye, RN
summary: PIV removed, vitals stable at 1400; ready for 1430 transport to Maple Grove with daughter's agreement.
body:
**Pre-transfer assessment**
Vitals 1400: T 98.6 F, HR 76, BP 130/70, RR 16, SpO2 96% on room air, pain 3/10. Oriented x4, calm. Scheduled acetaminophen 1,000 mg PO given at 1400.

**Lines**
Peripheral IV, 20 g left forearm, removed at 1415 with catheter intact, pressure held, small adhesive bandage; site clean without redness or swelling.

**Condition**
Right foot warm, pulses present, sensation intact; dressing dry and intact. Voiding spontaneously. Lungs clear.

**Transfer**
Patient is dressed and up in a wheelchair with glasses, left hearing aid and cane. Daughter Karen Mills at bedside and agrees with the plan. Wheelchair van transport scheduled for 1430 to Maple Grove; report already given to C. Pruitt, RN.

**Paperwork sent with patient**
- Transfer summary and medication list
- Discharge orders and MAR with last doses given
- Wound care and weight-bearing instructions
- Pending results (final urine culture, blood cultures)
- Follow-up appointments and Friday lab orders

Daughter will follow the van to Maple Grove and complete the facility paperwork.
